body:
### Screenshot

After switching from a landline to a mobile connection, one request failed with "API Error: Request blocked before it reached Anthropic's API (HTTP 403) · the  network this request came from isn't allowed". Resending the same message immediately succeeded on the same mobile connection. Region and account unchanged.

Attempts to send a feedback fail with error: "Couldn't send feedback (server returned 403: Request not allowed). If it keeps failing, you can file at https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues instead."


### What were you trying to do?

Send normal request after switching internet connection to mobile (because my landline connection failed).

### What happened instead?

I got an error:

> API Error: Request blocked before it reached Anthropic's API (HTTP 403) · the network this request came from isn't allowed: usually an unsupported region, or a VPN, proxy or hosting network · signing in again won't change this · check your VPN or network and retry · supported regions: https://anthropic.com/supported-countries

Sending it again passed. Attempt to send a feedback failed with error:

> Couldn't send feedback (server returned 403: Request not allowed). If it keeps failing, you can file at https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues instead.

```text

```

comments.body: Some of my messages fail with the same error, and passed next time.

Also I just got a message:

> Remote Control disconnected — a network edge refused the connection before it reached Anthropic's server (HTTP 403 — Anthropic's CDN enforcing a region or network policy, or a Cloudflare gateway on this network) rather than this session; this often follows a VPN or network change — run /remote-control to retry
It is difficult to work if my messages are randomly rejected. The last one was rejected 4 times of 5.
Even worse -- it is impossible to work, because any non-trivial request is interrupted in the middle after making a part of changes.

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **GPT-6.1 Sol responding on behalf of rogerArtefacto**

We are also seeing repeated Cloudflare HTTP 403 failures interrupting an established Claude Code session after successful model responses and tool execution. This is a related data point; the error wording differs from the original report, so we cannot yet establish that the underlying cause is identical.

Environment:

- Linux x86_64.
- Claude Code 2.1.322, verified both in the SDK session initialization events and with `claude --version`.
- Claude Code invoked through the Claude Agent SDK (`claude-agent-sdk.query`) inside T3 Code.
- Model: `claude-opus-5-5`; effort: high.
- SDK initialization reports `apiKeySource: "none"`. We have not independently established the credential mechanism from this field alone.

Observed sequence on November 13, 2026 (all times UTC):

1. The same conversation completed five runs successfully, with the last completing at approximately 10:14:30.
2. A subsequent run started at 10:15:55. Claude generated a response and executed read-only git/repository inspection commands. The tool completed successfully at 10:16:17.992.
3. The next provider request failed at 10:16:18.076 with:
   ```text
   Failed to authenticate. API Error: 403 Attention Required! | Cloudflare
   ```
4. We sent a follow-up asking about the failure at 10:18:51. Claude again generated a response and ran a read-only repository check successfully, completing the tool at 10:19:07.239.
5. The next provider request failed at 10:19:07.333 with the identical Cloudflare error.

Sanitized fields from the incoming SDK error event, present in both failures:
```json
{
  "type": "assistant",
  "error": "authentication_failed",
  "is_api_error_message": true,
  "api_error_status": 403,
  "api_error_origin": "first_party"
}
```

The SDK terminal result additionally reports:
```json
{
  "type": "result",
  "terminal_reason": "api_error",
  "is_error": true,
  "num_turns": 2,
  "api_error_status": 403,
  "api_error_origin": "first_party",
  "result": "Failed to authenticate. API Error: 403 Attention Required! | Cloudflare"
}
```

The SDK reported a credential expiration date of November 20, seven days after the failures. This does not prove credential validity, but the successful model requests immediately before each failure make simple credential expiry an incomplete explanation.

Impact: the conversation cannot finish the requested work reliably. Retrying a user turn gets far enough to run a tool, then fails when the provider is called again. The shell commands themselves complete successfully and do not return HTTP 403.

Limits of this report:

- This is an observed sequence, not a minimal standalone reproduction.
- We have not isolated whether the trigger is request content, network/IP policy, client behavior, or something else.
- No Cloudflare Ray ID, raw response headers, or blocked URL are exposed in the captured SDK events.
- We have not tested a different network, reauthentication, or a standalone CLI reproduction.

Could maintainers investigate these timestamps and clarify how to capture a Cloudflare Ray ID/request ID through the Agent SDK? Also, can this Cloudflare response be distinguished from a confirmed authentication failure in the emitted diagnostics? The current authentication label gives no indication of which layer rejected the request.

Private prompts, repository details, credentials, session identifiers, and full logs have been omitted.
